sentences.text:
Challenging judgment and award dated 03.05.2010 passed by Member M.A.C.T. No.III, Bagalkote,
in MVC no.177/2008, this appeal and cross objection are filed.
2. Brief facts as stated are that on 08.02.2008, Basavaraj Hampanna Ronad was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-29/L7952 from Bagalkot towards to Gudur to attend his duty at school.

On the way, near SC/ST hostel, on Bagalkot-Shirur road, driver of passenger auto bearing registration no.KA.29/6147 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle causing accident.
In accident, Basavaraj sustained grievous injuries and was taken to Dr.Kerudi Hospital, Bagalkot, but, died during treatment.

3. Alleging loss of dependency on account of his untimely death, his wife, three children and parents filed C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022 claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 against owner and insurer of auto rickshaw.
4. On service of summons, owner appeared and filed objection denying involvement of vehicle in accident and also alleged contributory negligence against deceased.
Insurer filed objection not only denying accident, but, also alleging violation of policy condition by insured.
It was contended that driver did not have valid and effective driving licence to drive particular class of vehicle and insurance policy was subject to vehicle holding valid permit etc.
5. Thereafter, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant no.3 as PW1 and another witness as PW2 and got marked Exhibits P.1 to P.6.
In rebuttal, official of insurer was examined as RW1.
Owner of vehicle was examined as RW2.
Exs.R1 to R6 were marked.
6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of auto by its C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022 driver.

It assessed total compensation of Rs.11,77,400/-
with interest at 6% p.a. against insurer
Aggrieved by said award, insurer is in appeal challenging finding of tribunal regarding involvement of vehicle, liability as well as quantum.

In said appeal,
claimants have filed cross objection for enhancement of compensation.

7. Shri G.N.Raichur, learned counsel for insurer submitted that claim petition was earlier dismissed and remanded by this Court in MFA no.20199/2010 with liberty to claimant to examine owner of vehicle and to lead evidence regarding involvement of vehicle.
After remand, claimants examined one of charge-sheet witness as PW2, while insurer examined owner-cum-driver of vehicle as RW2.
It was submitted that RW2 specifically stated that his vehicle was not involved in accident.
It was submitted that accident allegedly occurred on 08.02.2008, vehicle was seized on 13.02.2008, which would indicate possibility of false implication.
It was submitted that without properly considering deposition of RW2, tribunal held insured C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022 vehicle having caused accident and awarded compensation.
Even on quantum, it was submitted that tribunal awarded excessive compensation.

It was submitted that though as per Ex.P6, professional tax of Rs.150/- was mentioned, while calculating compensation, tribunal failed to deduct said sum from gross income and thereby committed error.

The Oriental Insurnce Co. Ltd vs Drakshyani W/O. Basavaraj Ronad on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95556391/
4 8.

sentences.text: On other hand Shri S.C.Hiremath, learned counsel for claimant-cross objectors submitted that impugned award insofar as involvement of vehicle and liability of insurer was fully justified and insurer's appeal was without merit.

Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that tribunal committed error in not adding future prospects and awarding inadequate compensation under conventional heads and sought for enhancement.
9. From above submission, it is not in dispute that Basavaraj Hampanna Ronad died in motor vehicle accident on 08.02.2008.

While insurer contends that death was on account of own negligence of deceased and insurer was C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022 not liable, claimants contend that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle and claimants were entitled for compensation from insurer and even assessment of compensation is questioned.
Therefore, following points that would arise for consideration:
"1. Whether finding of tribunal regarding involvement of vehicle and liability of insurer is justified ?
2. Whether assessment of compensation by tribunal calls for modification as sought for?"

POINT NO.1:
10. Re-false implication of vehicle:

To establish rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle by its driver, claimants produced copy of FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, MVI report and charge-sheet marked as Exs.P1 to P3 and P5 respectively.
They have also examined eye witness as PW2.

Perusal of Exs.P1 and P2 would indicate that complaint is filed by son of C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022 deceased who stated that incident occurred at 5:30 a.m. while complaint is given at 12:30 p.m on same day.
In complaint, vehicle number is clearly mentioned.
In Ex.P3- spot panchanama, seizure of broken indicator parts is mentioned.

In Ex.P6-MVI report, damages noted on auto- rickshaw are as follows:
i) Right side head light and indicator damaged.
ii) Right side front body shape damaged.
11.
Ex.P4-P.M report indicates cause of death as due to road traffic accident.
Ex. P5
-charge-sheet is registered against owner-cum-driver of vehicle.
It would also indicate name of PW2 as one of charge-sheet witness.

In examination-in-chief affidavit, RW2 has stated as follows:
"That it is true to say that I am the owner of tomtom vehicle bearing No.KA.29/6147 falsly involved in this accident, but there is no negligent acts attributed by me in driving the vehicle but clear and absolute negligent acts attributed on the part of The Oriental Insurnce Co. sentences.text: deceased
Basavaraj Ronad who came on wrong side of road, hence, I am not liable to pay any of the compensation amount to the petitioners."
Even in his objection, there is similar assertion.

PW2 in his deposition has stated that on date of accident while he was returning from his field, he saw deceased riding his motorcycle on left side of road while driver of auto-rickshaw came on wrong side and dashed against motorcyclist.
Though suggestions are made about false implication of vehicle, same are denied.

In view of clear statement by owner about involvement of his vehicle in accident and taking a stand alleging contributory negligence against deceased, it would not lie in mouth of insured to contend that insured vehicle was not at all involved in accident.
However, it would be a different matter whether contributory negligence is alleged.
Insofar as contributory negligence, it is seen from Ex.P.3 that accident occurred on a 22 feet wide road with 5 feet kachcha road on either side.
Motorcycle was found lying on one feet from northern edge at 21 feet from southern edge of road.
Broken pieces of indicator of two wheeler and auto-rickshaw are also found at said spot.

When said material is considered in light of charge-sheet registered - 11 - C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022 against driver of insured vehicle, finding of tribunal regarding negligence and involvement of vehicle would be fully justified.
Contention of insurer is without any merit.
13. It is also contended that driving license held by driver was not valid and effective to drive vehicle.
It is seen that vehicle involved as per Ex.R4 is a passenger auto-rickshaw.
Ex.R6-Driving license is issued authorizing him to drive auto-rickshaw.
Even said contention is without any merit.
14. Accordingly, point no.1 is answered in negative.

POINT NO.2:
15.
Insofar as quantum of compensation, from Ex.P6 Rs.150/- is stated to be towards professional tax.
Same has to be deducted.
However, tribunal has not added any amount towards future prospects.
Tribunal also erred in not awarding any compensation towards personal expenses.

Thus,
there is error on quantum of compensation.
Deceased was 58 years of age and Government school teacher
. Claimants are wife, three children and parents.
However, mother is subsequently deleted.
Thus, there are five dependents.

As per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and The Oriental Insurnce Co. Ltd vs Drakshyani W/O. Basavaraj Ronad on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95556391/
6 others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, '15%' has to be added towards future prospects, deduction towards personal expenses would be '1/4th' and multiplier applicable would be '9'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rs.150/- is also required to be deducted from gross salary of Rs.10,774/-.

Thus, loss of dependency would be:
'Rs.10,624/- + 15% - 1/4th x 12 x 9= Rs.9,89,625/-.'
17.

In addition, claimant no.1 would be entitled for compensation towards loss of spousal consortium, claimants no.2 to 4 would be entitled to compensation towards loss of parental consortium, claimant no.5 would be entitled to compensation towards loss of filial consortium at Rs.40,000/- each, i.e., Rs.2,00,000/ in total.
- 13 - C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022 They would also be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
Since more than three years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), they would be entitled to addition of 10% towards award under conventional heads, i.e., Rs.23,000/-.

Thus, total compensation would be:
"Rs.9,89,625/- + Rs.2,53,000/- = Rs.12,42,625/- as against Rs.11,77,400/- awarded by tribunal."
Point No.2 for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.
18. In result, I pass following:
ORDER i
) M.F.A no.22906/2013 is dismissed.
ii) M.F.A Crob.no.100012/2022 is allowed in part.

iii) Judgment and award dated 03.05.2013, passed by Member, MACT-III, Bagalkote,
in MVC no.177/2008 is modified.

- 14 -  C/W MFA.CROB No. 100012 of 2022  iv) Claimants are held entitled for  reassessed compensation of  Rs.12,42,625/- as against The Oriental Insurnce Co. Ltd vs Drakshyani W/O. Basavaraj Ronad on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95556391/
7  Rs.11,77,400/- awarded by tribunal  along with interest at rate of 6% p.a.
from date of claim petition till date of deposit.
